model.description: Its id, as the harness spells it.

provider.description: Its provider, as the harness spells it.

thinking.description: The thinking levels it takes, in the harness's own words.

Models.description: `models`: the models that the harness runs here. Its parameters are [`super::Empty`].

models.description: Each listed model, with the harness's default first.

signed_in.description:
Whether the harness's own account is signed in here at the time of this list, as
the harness says. `true`: signed in. `false`: not signed in. Absent where the driver
cannot tell.

unlisted.description: The harness also runs models that it does not list.

watch.description: The files that change the list when they change.

Moment.description: A moment where the harness stopped.

context_left.description: The share of the context window left, 0 to 1.

continued.description: At a `turn_end`: a hook already made this turn continue once.

event.description: The hook event of the moment.

failure.description: At a `turn_end` whose `outcome` is `failed`: the cause, where the harness gives it.

model.description:
The model that the conversation runs on now, where the moment gives it. This is
state, never an event.

outcome.description: At a `turn_end`: how the turn ended.

person_exited.description: At a `session_end`: the person exited at the prompt.

sub_agent.description: The sub-agent whose moment it is.

suggestions.description:
At a `permission`: the harness's own ways to allow such calls from now on, in its
order. `always: {suggestion: n}` is the n-th.

thinking.description:
The thinking level now, in the harness's own word, where the moment gives it. This
is state, never an event.

transcript.description: Its transcript, where the harness keeps it outside its own folders.

Named.description: A host, as `hosts/ensure` and `hosts/fork` answer it.

Need.description:
What a harness lacks on this host that only its person can give, and the ways that the
person can give it.

id.description:
The id of this need, the same in every plan (`sign-in`). `needs/give` names the need
by this id.

line.description: What is missing and what it stops, in one line.

title.description: The card's title: a short question its person answers (`Sign Claude Code in?`).

ways.description:
Each way that the person can give it, with the driver's preferred way first. At
least one.

NeedLink.description: A page that the person opens for a way.

fills.description:
The field that the return address of the page fills. Only where the page sends the
browser back to a loopback address, and the app that opened the page receives it.

Notified.description: `host/notified`: a program's notification, from the host.

Opened.description: `host/opened`: the listener of the host accepted a connection.

Optional.description: An optional method of an adapter that makes hosts, by the last word of its name.

Os.description: An operating system an adapter provides.

Part.description: What reaches a harness through a setup entry.

oneOf.description: Steery's MCP entry.
Steery's skill.
The hooks that run `<hook> <event>`.
Steery's plugin, which connects to the door.

paths.description: The absolute path of each file.

Pick.description: `pick`: a model and thinking for a running conversation.

model.description: The model, as the harness spells it.

thinking.description: The thinking level, in the harness's own word.

Picked.description: The model and thinking that a conversation runs on, as the driver read them back.

Plan.description: What installs the runtime as a service. The runtime writes the files and runs the commands.

commands.description:
The commands to run after the files, in order. When a command that must not fail
fails, the runtime does not run the rest.

may_fail.description: When this command fails, the plan continues.

Planned.description: The harness that the driver found here, and the entries that configure it.

entries.description: What the runtime writes into the harness, and nothing else.

found.description: The harness, where it is installed here; absent where it is not.

install.description:
The vendor's own installer for the harness. Present only where the harness is not
installed here (`found` absent) and its driver can install it.

needs.description:
What the harness lacks here that only its person can give, for example a sign-in or
a setting. Steery asks for each need on one card, and the runtime gives the answer
back by `needs/give`. Version 5 only: empty in an older version.

notes.description: Lines for a person about the setup.

refused.description: Why Steery does not configure this harness here, in one line.

oneOf.description: The first frame. The plugin sends it within 5 s.

cwd.description: The folder that the conversation runs in, as the harness has it now.

door.description: The door version the plugin speaks.

harness.description: The id of a driver whose door is `plugin`.

lead.description: The conversation that the copy of a sub-agent works in.

session_id.description: The conversation that this copy is in. For a sub-agent, the sub-agent's own id.

oneOf.description: The whole state, when it changes.

A moment of a hook with `via: door`: the harness's own payload. The runtime reads it
with `hook/read`, as it reads the document of a command hook. The runtime reads each
moment `id` once.

document.description: The harness's hook payload, as the plugin got it.

oneOf.description: A turn that the copy itself ran ended.

asked.description: The turn asked its person something.

continued.description: The plugin already continued this turn once.

waiting.description: The turn waits on a Steery request.

oneOf.description:
The answer to an ask: `ok` with the answer of the op, or `refused` with the line of the
harness.

The records of the harness after `after`, in the order that the harness appended them.
The plugin sends them only on a connection that the runtime welcomed with `entries`.

after.description:
The id of the record before the first record in this frame. Absent: these records
start at the first record of the conversation.

oneOf.description:
The copy cannot continue from `welcome.entries.after`: this connection carries no
entries.

The message of the agent while the agent writes it. The plugin sends it only on a
connection that the runtime welcomed with `live`.

at.description: The time of the newest piece, in milliseconds since 1970 on the harness's clock.

end.description: The message ended: every part of it came before this frame or in it.

first_at.description: The time of the first piece of this message, on the same clock.

forming.description:
The tool that a call names while the agent forms the call, before the agent sends its
input.

message.description:
The harness's key for the message. It stays the same from the first frame to the last.
It is the identity of the reply, as `words.message` names it in the record.

ProcessEnded.description: How a process that `process/start` started ended, as its `status` file holds it.

oneOf.description: It exited with this code.
A signal ended it.

args.description:
Its arguments, with its own name first. Absent where the adapter cannot read them.
Then the process can be any program.

cwd.description: The folder that it works in now. Absent where the adapter cannot read it.

process_start.description: Its start time, in milliseconds since 1970.

service.description: The service manager that keeps the runtime in operation.

pids.description: Only these pids. Absent: every process.

processes.description:
Each process that runs, with no zombie. Where no process has a pid in `pids`, that pid
is absent.

ProcessStart.description: `process/start`: start a process detached, in a session and process group of its own.

cwd.description: The folder that the process runs in.

env.description: The whole environment of the process.

held.description:
The standard input of the process never ends, and `stdin` is absent. An adapter
refuses `invalid` where the request sets both.

scope.description:
The label of the service whose share of the CPU the process runs in, where there is
one.

started.description:
The `<what>` of `STEERY_STARTED`. The adapter sets `STEERY_STARTED=<its own pid>:<what>`
in the environment of the process. This value replaces any value that `env` gives it.

status.description:
The file where the adapter writes how the process ended ([`Ended`]), at mode 0600. The
adapter writes it when it reaps the process.

stderr.description: The file that the adapter appends the standard error of the process to.

stdin.description: The file that its standard input reads. Absent: none.

stdout.description: The file that the adapter appends the standard output of the process to.

files.description:
Its build for each target, by Rust target triple: `aarch64-apple-darwin`,
`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. At least one.

kind.description: The kind that its `initialize` answers: `harness` for a driver, `machine` for an adapter.

ProgramInfo.description:
Who a program is, and how a person sees it. Each surface where Steery draws a harness or a
machine reads these fields and nothing else.

id.description:
For a driver, the id that `Session.harness` names. For an adapter, the id that a
machine names as its adapter.

label.description:
Its name as a person reads it, one line of at most [`Self::LABEL_MAX`] characters:
`Claude Code`, `Daytona`.

mark.description:
Its mark: the `d` of one SVG path in a 24 by 24 box, at most [`Self::MARK_MAX`] bytes.
Surfaces fill the path with the even-odd rule. Absent: the tile shows `short`.

short.description: Its name on a tile, one to [`Self::SHORT_MAX`] characters: `CC`.

tint.description: Its colour on a tile, `#rrggbb` in lowercase. Absent: Steery's neutral tint.

Programs.description:
What `host/programs` answers: the programs of the host, each as it answered `initialize`.
For each program that does not run, it also says why `serve` cannot start it.

drivers.description: The drivers of the host that run.

missing.description: The drivers of the host that `serve` cannot start, each with why.

os.description: The operating-system adapter of the host.

Put.description: `hosts/put`: write a file into a host. Its result is [`super::Empty`].

content.description: The whole content of the file, base64.

host.description: The adapter's id for the host.

mode.description: The Unix mode bits of the file.

path.description: The absolute path of the file inside the host.

Question.description: A question that a call asks the person.

multiple.description: The person can choose more than one option.

anyOf.description: A local command whose standard input and output are the channel.

env.description: The variables to add to the environment of the command.

anyOf.description: The adapter carries the bytes itself, as `stream/*` messages with this id.

Reach.description: How a channel reaches its command.

Read.description: `sessions/read`: a conversation's events after a cursor.

cursor.description: Where the last read or fold ended; absent: from the beginning.

sub_agent.description: One of its sub-agents, to read in place of the conversation.

tail.description: Read only the newest records within this many bytes of the end.

ReadAs.description: How the runtime reads a reader's output.

oneOf.description: The whole output is the answer.
The output goes to `reader/read`.

Reader.description: `reader`: a launch plan for a read that runs once.

asked.description: The text that the reader reads.

model.description: The model, as the harness spells it; absent: the harness's own.

system.description: The instructions; absent: the harness's own.

thinking.description:
The thinking level, as the driver's `models` spells it for that model. Absent: the
driver's own level for a read. A level that the harness refuses gives
`selection-unsupported`.

tools.description: The tools that it can use.

known.description: Models that the reader runs, which `models` possibly does not list.

unnamed.description: The reader runs the harness's own model when it gets no model.

ReaderFile.description: A file that a reader's plan writes first.

env.description: The variables it adds to the environment.

files.description: Files that the runtime writes first, relative to `cwd`.

read.description: How the runtime reads its output.

stdin.description: `words`: the runtime writes `asked` to its standard input.

ReaderRead.description: `reader/read`: a reader's output, to read as its answer.

ReaderTools.description: The tools that a reader can use.

owner.description: The owner token of the turn that took them.

ReceiptFind.description: `receipt/find`: the input that carries a delivery marker, after a mark.

ReceiptMark.description: `receipt/mark`: a point in a conversation before the runtime sends words.

Record.description: One record of a conversation as the harness keeps it: its id, and its value verbatim.

value.description:
The record. Absent where it is over [`super::door::RECORDS_MAX`]: then the driver
reads it from the transcript by `id`.

Runtime.description: The runtime a program runs under.

arch.description: The processor architecture, as Rust names it: `x86_64`, `aarch64`.

os.description: The operating system it runs on, as Rust names it: `linux`, `macos`.

oneOf.description:
The runtime accepted the hello. `entries`: this runtime takes the records of the
harness. `live`: it takes `live` frames.
The answer to a moment or a settle.
Something the runtime asks of the copy.

Words into the conversation. The copy answers with [`DoorSaid`] when the harness holds
the words. When the runtime asks again under the same `id` while the harness holds
them, the copy answers when the harness took them.

idle.description:
Only when the conversation is idle. Else the copy refuses with `harness-busy` and
gives nothing to the harness.

throw.description: The words of one throw go in only once.

oneOf.description: A model and thinking. The copy answers with [`super::harness::Picked`].

Stop the turn that runs now. The copy answers with [`DoorStopped`]. Without `say`, this
is the person's pause.

Force the words of `say` in now. The harness holds these words and did not take them yet.

1. The copy aborts the turn that runs now. It does not park the conversation.
2. The harness takes the words as its next input.
3. The copy gives again, once, the words that the harness let go with the abort.

The copy answers with [`DoorStopped`].

Forget everything before a cut, and keep `summary` in its place. The copy answers with
[`DoorCompacted`].

Said.description: Whether the driver saw the harness take the words.

took.description: False: the driver gave the words but has no confirmation.

Sample.description: What a driver can prove of a conversation now.

error.description: The harness's own line, where it failed.

if_unheld.description: This sample is true only if no process holds the conversation.

vacant.description: Nobody is in the conversation at all.

sample.description: What the driver can prove now; absent: it cannot say.

id.description:
The name of the say (version 7): the delivery that its words carry, else a name of
the runtime's own. The driver names it in `turn.says` of the turn that took the words.

mode.description: When the words go into the conversation.

SayMode.description: When the words of a `say` go into the conversation.

oneOf.description: Into the running turn.
After the running turn.
Only where nothing runs.

Says.description: A paragraph a moment can give the agent.

oneOf.description:
Steery's paragraph for the conversation. At a `turn_end`, it makes the agent
continue. At a `sub_agent_start`, it goes to the sub-agent.
A notice that words wait for the agent.
A line about the shell command a call runs.
A paragraph for a sub-agent in the middle of its work.

Sealed.description: What a reader blocks (true) or can still reach (false).

sent.description: False where the pid no longer has that start time.

ServicePlan.description: `service/plan`: what installs the runtime as a service. The method is pure.

cpu.description: The share of the runtime, 1 to 100 percent, of what the computer grants its user.

log.description: The file that the service appends its own output to.

port.description: The service manager gives the runtime the listener of this loopback port.

Session.description: One conversation in the harness's store.

app.description: It started in the harness's app.

parent.description: The conversation that this one is a fork of.

sub_agents.description: The sub-agents that work in it.

transcripts.description:
Every file of it on this host, oldest first. At least one where the harness keeps
transcript files (`HarnessInfo.transcript`), and none where it does not.

SessionChanged.description:
`session/changed`: a notification that a driver with its own door sends without a
request.

SessionRef.description: A conversation, by its driver and its id.

SessionsTouched.description:
`sessions/touched`: a notification that a driver whose facts say `touches` sends without
a request, one for each change that it saw (version [`crate::TOUCHES`]).

external_ids.description:
The conversations whose thread, or a thread of one of whose sub-agents, changed.
[`SessionsTouched::EVERY`] names every conversation that the driver listed.

Setting.description: A setting a program needs a person to give once.

about.description: One line for a person: what it is and where to find it.

required.description: The program does not run without it.

secret.description: The runtime keeps it in its private config folder and never shows it again.

Setup.description: `setup/plan`: what the runtime writes to configure the harness for Steery.

door.description: The runtime's loopback door URL, which a `plugin` door connects to.

hook.description:
The command line that a hook runs. The driver adds the hook's event as one more
argument.

timeout.description: The seconds that an MCP entry gives one call.

trusts.description:
Folders where a harness can run here as if its person trusted them. This applies to
a harness that runs only in a folder that a person trusted. The folders are those of
a host that an adapter made for its conversations. Nobody opens the terminal of that
host to answer the harness's prompt. Empty on a person's own computer, where the
person trusts a folder themselves.

SetupFacts.description: The facts for the setup of a harness and for its MCP calls.

call_bound.description:
The longest time that the harness waits for one MCP call, in seconds, when no entry can
make this time longer.

cuts_tool_text.description:
The harness cuts the description of an MCP tool before its model reads it. So
`session_start` gives the whole escalation policies.

reads_skills.description:
True: the harness reads Steery's skill from the entry that `setup/plan` lists. False:
the MCP handshake carries the whole skill.

Signal.description: `process/signal`: send a signal to a process, only where the pid still has that start time.

group.description: Send the signal to its whole process group.

process_start.description: Its start time. The pid must still have this start time.

SignalName.description: A signal that the runtime sends.

Source.description: What an adapter makes a host from.

oneOf.description: A vendor's snapshot, by name.
A container image, by reference.

The whole text of a Dockerfile. The vendor builds it in its owner's account. The same
bytes give the same build. Only where the adapter's facts say `builds`.

Spoken.description: The runtime's answer to a moment or a settle.

say.description: A paragraph for the agent. After a settle, the plugin uses it to make the agent continue.

Start.description: `start`: the launch plan of a turn. It starts nothing.

external_id.description: The conversation that the turn continues or forks.

folder.description: The turn's folder, which the runtime made.

model.description: The model, as the harness spells it.

reads.description: Folders outside `cwd` that the turn reads.

thinking.description: The thinking level, in the harness's own word.

worktree.description: Run a fork or a new conversation in a new worktree.

process_start.description: Its start time, in milliseconds since 1970.

Stat.description: What is at a path. `serve` does not follow a link.

granted.description: The percent of one core the computer grants the runtime's user.

pid.description: The process that the service runs as.

Stdin.description: What a launch's standard input carries.

oneOf.description: The words.
Nothing.

Nothing, and no end: the process takes its words through its live door and runs
until something stops it.

Stop.description: `stop`: the harness's own way to end a turn. The runtime's signals come after it.

say.description:
The `id` of a `say` (version 7). Stop only the turn that its words began. Refuse
`other-turn` where another turn runs. Absent: the person's stop.

Stopped.description: What the graceful step of `stop` did.

proof.description: The driver's one line of evidence: the turn it ended and the state it reached.

stopped.description:
This step ended the turn. For a `process` holder, the runtime signals the process
after this step where it still runs, whatever this field says.

Stream.description: One of a process's output streams.

StreamClosed.description: `stream/closed`: the adapter says that a channel ended.

exit.description: The command's exit code, where it has one.

StreamData.description: `stream/data`: the bytes of the command, which the adapter sends.

StreamWrite.description: `stream/write`: the bytes that the runtime sends to a channel.

SubAgent.description: A sub-agent that works in a conversation.

lead.description: The sub-agent that started it; absent: the conversation's own agent did.

started_by.description: The id of the call that started it.

task.description: The first line of the task that it got.

transcripts.description: Every file of it, oldest first.

Suggestion.description: One of the harness's own ways to allow such calls from now on, as a person reads it.

about.description: One line about its scope: `this project, for you`.

label.description: What a person reads for it: `Always Bash(cargo check:*)`.

oneOf.description: The whole filesystem.
The filesystem and the memory.
Only the folder in `persist`.

Terminal.description: `terminal`: the command that opens a conversation in a terminal.

app.description: The URL that opens it in the harness's app.

command.description: The command line, quoted for a POSIX shell.

line.description: What a person reads about it.

ended.description: How the turn ends, unless a later line says otherwise.

events.description:
The events of the named conversation that this line gives. Each has the id that
`sessions/read` gives the same fact.

named.description: The conversation that the harness named.

refused.description: The refusal word that a line of standard error means.

title.description: The title that the harness gave the named conversation.

TurnRead.description: `turn/read`: one line that a turn's process wrote.

delivery.description: The name of the delivery marker that the runtime put in the words.

turn.description: The run that the line belongs to. A driver can keep state across its lines.

oneOf.description: The harness wrote no end and its process is gone, or something stopped it.

Unlisted.description: What a model takes when the harness does not list it.

thinking.description: Its thinking levels, in the harness's own words.

values.description: Each variable that has a value, by name. A variable with no value is absent.

Via.description: How a moment reaches the runtime.

oneOf.description: The harness runs `<hook> <event>` with its document on standard input.
The plugin sends it over the door (§4.4).

Voice.description: Who said words in a conversation.

oneOf.description: What a person typed.
The agent's answer.
The agent's reasoning or progress, where the harness writes it as text.

The text of a call's result, after its `call_ended`. The input of a call is in
`call_began.call.input`, and the driver never repeats it as words.
A harness's summary of earlier history.

Way.description: One way a person gives what a harness lacks.

about.description: Its cost or risk, in one line.

ends_at.description:
When the state that this way holds ends (for example, a sign-in that the driver
started for it), in milliseconds since 1970 (§2).

fields.description: The values that the person types. The runtime gives each one back by its `name`.

id.description: The id of this way of its need, the same in every plan (`api-key`).

label.description: What it does, in a few plain words (`Use your API key`).

link.description:
The page that the person opens first: the page that makes a key, or an authorize
page.
